selected_news.title: Perseverence Marsta Işıklı Gabbro Kayalarını Keşfetti
selected_news.summary: Explore This Section Perseverance Home Mission Overview Rover Components Mars Rock Samples Where is Perseverance? Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Mission Updates Science Overview Objectives Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Perseverance Raw Images Images Videos Audio More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home NASA’s Perseverance rover acquired this image of some light-toned boulders scattered across a hillside of a region called “Lac de Charmes,” beyond the western rim of Jezero crater. Perseverance captured the image using its Right Mastcam-Z camera on Aug. 30, 2026 (Sol 1965, or Martian day 1,965 of the Mars 2020 mission) at the local mean solar time of 11:42:55. NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU Written by Alex Jones, Ph.D. candidate at Imperial College London Sept. 29, 2026 After spending the last six months exploring “ Lac de Charmes ,” a region of ancient rock beyond Jezero crater’s western rim, Perseverance has stumbled upon a vast field of light-toned rocks peppering the Martian surface. Light-colored rocks are a strange sight on Mars , a planet dominated by dark-colored basaltic rocks. This many light-colored rocks in one place piqued the Science Team’s interest… what are they? How did they get here? To answer the first question, Perseverance has been investigating the composition and textures of these rocks. Data so far indicates that many of them are igneous rocks called gabbro, which are dominated by minerals rich in iron and magnesium. Such rocks typically form by slow cooling and crystallization of magma deep in the crust. So how did these deep fragments of Mars find their way to the surface? Perseverance has spent the last week trying to answer this question by investigating a patch of possible bedrock poking out between the light-toned boulders and loose regolith. Initial images suggest that the rock is made up of light- and dark-colored, angular fragments of rock, forming what geologists call a breccia. One possibility the team is investigating is that the light-toned boulders scattered across the hillside have eroded out of this breccia. Perseverance deploys its arm mounted instruments to investigate a possible breccia outcrop at “Idubi.” The rover acquired this image of the area in front of it using its onboard Front Right Hazard Avoidance Camera A on Sept. 27, 2026 (Sol 1992, or Martian day 1,992 of the Mars 2020 mission) at the local mean solar time of 12:03:10. NASA/JPL-Caltech Breccias often form through violent processes involving the fracturing and transport of rock to produce their angular shapes. Layers of breccia observed outside Jezero have previously been attributed to asteroid impacts on early Mars . Perhaps similar impacts (or the Jezero impact itself?) could be responsible for digging up these light-colored blocks. Only time (and of course, Perseverance), will tell. selected_news.summary: Opposition leader says Coalition would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor says a Coalition government would cut net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years, calling the plan “the biggest cut to immigration in the history” of Australia. Following moves by One Nation and Labor to capitalise on growing anti-migration sentiment, the opposition leader announced plans by the Liberals and Nationals on Tuesday, promising net overseas migration rates of 130,000 in the third year and 160,000 in the fourth. Tougher screening of visa applicants. Revising the temporary skilled priority list. Establishing a strike force to clear the backlog of skilled construction applications to address workforce shortages. Doubling the talent and innovation allocation to 7,000 places, through a new Aukus and Five Eyes visa. Linking each student visa to the enrolling institution. selected_news.summary: Comedian reveals cancer in a joke-packed video, saying she will undergo a double mastectomy and ‘I’ll be keeping you abreast of everything, Australia’ Comedian and actor Judith Lucy has revealed she has been diagnosed with breast cancer. In a video shared to Instagram on Tuesday afternoon, the 58-year-old said she had “a little, not-so-fun update” to share. Continue reading...
selected_news.article_text: Comedian reveals cancer in a joke-packed video, saying she will undergo a double mastectomy and ‘I’ll be keeping you abreast of everything, Australia’ Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email Comedian and actor Judith Lucy has revealed she has been diagnosed with breast cancer In a video shared to Instagram on Tuesday afternoon, the 58-year-old said she had “a little, not-so-fun update” to share “I got an email from BreastScreen Australia, telling me that my mammogram result was a bit weird. May I take this opportunity to say, ladies, for the love of God, keep up with your mammograms,” she said. “Long story short, I’ve got breast cancer.” Lucy said she went for a lumpectomy last week, when “a doctor – I’m not making this up – called Doctor Fun found more cancer” Lucy said the cancer was early stage and “relatively non-aggressive”. She said that though cancer had been detected in one of her breasts, she would soon undergo a double mastectomy to remove both Sign up for our rundown of must-reads, pop culture and tips for the weekend, every Sunday morning “Doctor Fun is amazing. I am in her debt, but we have gone from a lumpectomy to a mastectomy, which I am having Friday week,” she said “I said, while you’re there, let’s get rid of the other one because you know something. I have had 40 years of, if I do say so myself, large and spectacular breasts. You had your chance, fellas,” she said. “I think I’m quite fine with going bra-free for my last chapter. And my last chapter is going to be very long and healthy.” Earlier this month Lucy published her latest book, Well Well Well, about her lifelong fascination with the wellness industry “There’s nothing like releasing a book about wellness as you’re being diagnosed with breast cancer. Now, fortunately the book does not end with me going, ‘And I’ve never been healthier!’ In fact, kinda the point of the book is that there are no quick fixes and we should all just be living differently,” she said Lucy read a passage from the book’s intro: “I know how lucky I am to not have a more serious health condition.
